01. Have you attached the required transcript(s) with conferral date/s of the degree/s to your application? Failure to provide unofficial transcripts of all degrees listed in your application will result in an incomplete application. Options: Yes | No

02. Do you possess degree(s) earned from an institution outside of the United States? NOTE: If yes, you will be required to upload an evaluation and translation (foreign transcript evaluation). A list of approved organizations can be found in the job announcement. Failure to provide this foreign transcript evaluation will result in an incomplete application. Options: Yes | No
Develop and implement strategies to build and sustain public-private partnerships (PPPs) that benefit the district academically, vocationally, and financially
Build and maintain relationships with community partners, non-profit organizations, for-profit businesses, and industry leaders to enhance student learning and align with district goals
Lead efforts to explore and adopt innovative practices that foster new systems and enterprises for the district, embracing non-traditional models where applicable
Assist with fundraising efforts, including identifying and securing grants and foundations that align with the district’s master planning and diversification goals
Work closely with legal counsel and experts to ensure contracts and partnerships comply with local, state, and federal regulations
Provide leadership for academic enterprise services, including the Merced College Business Resource Center, contract education, community services, and related programs
Collaborate with district administration to ensure that special projects, contracts, and PPPs align with district goals and are adequately supported
Develop comprehensive plans to diversify the district's funding streams through new ventures, innovations, and enterprise systems

Lead the design, implementation, and evaluation of programs and services related to contract education, special training and contracted workforce development, and community services, ensuring alignment with district goals and industry standards
Promote shared governance through active participation in college and district committees
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of emerging trends, innovations, and best practices in community college education, public-private partnerships, and funding diversification
Prepare reports on programs and activities, ensuring compliance with federal and state mandates and alignment with district strategic objectives
Manage the area budget, ensuring financial resources are used effectively and in accordance with district policies
Resolve student, faculty, and staff conflicts and issues within the area
Evaluate faculty, administrators, and classified staff in accordance with district policies and collective bargaining agreements
Encourage cultural and ethnic diversity in staffing, curriculum, programs, and services.
Perform related duties as assigned
Higher education in community colleges, including the mission of the California Community Colleges
Establish and maintain productive and constructive relationships with students, administrators, faculty, and staff from diverse cultural and socio-economic backgrounds.
Public-private partnerships and innovative funding models in higher education
Train, select, direct, supervise, and evaluate personnel
Contract education, workforce development, and community service programs
Collaborate with faculty and industry partners to develop and modify programs and initiatives that meet student and community needs
Strategic enrollment management
Analyze, interpret, apply, and explain laws, regulations, labor contracts, policies, and procedures
Curriculum development and course articulation
Analyze situations accurately and adopt an effective course of action
Budget preparation and control
Plan, organize, and implement multiple projects and programs, providing regular updates to the Vice President of External Relations
District organization, operations, policies, and objectives
Compile and present narrative and statistical reports in a concise and comprehensive manner
Community college business management, including budgeting, grants, auditing accounts, and faculty load accounting
Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions, and implement recommendations in support of goals
Principles and practices of administration, supervision, and training
Emerging technologies and trends in teaching, learning, and instructional operations
Methods and techniques of program development and administration
Principles and procedures of report preparation
Successful interpersonal skills, organizational leadership, team building, staff development, and communication techniques
Communicate effectively both verbally and in writing with faculty, staff, students, and community members
Maintain current knowledge of program rules, regulations, requirements, and restrictions

Promote and incorporate culturally affirming DEIA and anti-racist principles to nurture and create a respectful, inclusive, and equitable learning and work environment. In conducting their duties, staff members shall respect and acknowledge the diversity of students and colleagues
